transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-19 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam O'Neill (Redwood) - Ravi Patel, Sofia Martinez, Jordan Lee (EdgeScale)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda: scoping the benchmark harness integration, what scripts you have, clarify success criteria and timelines.
[00:18] Ravi Patel: yeah thanks Maya. we've got about 30 minutes to go through the workload, do some qualification. Sofia and Jordan will cover the details.
[00:35] Sofia Martinez: hi all. to start, our main ask is to validate that Redwood can meet our p95 latency SLO of 300ms for short interactive calls and sustain X rps for a production subset. we use a mix of streaming chat and non-streaming completions.
[00:52] Liam O'Neill: when you say short interactive calls, what's the token distribution? avg prompt tokens and completion tokens?
[01:05] Sofia Martinez: good question — avg prompt is ~40 tokens, completion about 80 tokens for the assistant, but we also have long context cases up to 2k tokens for some retrieval-augmented flows. most traffic though is the short 40/80 pattern.
[01:24] Maya Chen: ok that's helpful. for benchmarking we'll want representative scripts that mirror that distribution. we typically ask customers to provide 3 sample scripts: interactive short, medium context, and long-RAG like flow.
[01:40] Ravi Patel: can you run both streaming and non-streaming tests? streaming is important because we care about time-to-first-byte as well as end-to-end.
[01:52] Liam O'Neill: yes we can. there's a couple of gotchas: streaming adds connection overhead and affects how we batch. our harness supports both modes; for streaming we measure ttfb, chunk latency, and final completion time. for non-streaming we look at p50/p95/p99 end-to-end.
[02:12] Jordan Lee: are you recommending any specific load test tool? we already use Locust internally, but can also export k6.
[02:22] Maya Chen: Locust is fine — we have example Locust scripts that plug into our harness. we also provide a lightweight python runner that replays customer scripts with exact tokenization to ensure token accounting.
[02:38] Sofia Martinez: nice. how do you handle stateful flows where KV cache benefits matter? our RAG flows rely on caching between requests.
[02:48] Liam O'Neill: good point. we can simulate warm and cold cache runs. for warm-cache, the harness will pre-populate the KV for a subset of users and measure gain; for cold-cache we'll measure baseline. note that streaming + cache interaction can slightly change throughput numbers.
[03:05] Speaker 1: (mumbled) and there's quantization impact on latency, did I hear that right?
[03:11] Liam O'Neill: yes — quantization profiles matter. for initial runs we'll run a couple of model configs: fp16 baseline, int8 quantized, and a mid-point if needed. that'll give you cost vs latency tradeoffs.
[03:25] Ravi Patel: ok budget-wise we need to compare unit cost per 1M tokens across those configs. can the harness estimate cost?
[03:33] Maya Chen: we output per-token latency and usage metrics; we also have a simple cost model approximator. we'll give you the raw metrics and a recommended cost breakdown.
[03:44] Sofia Martinez: what about concurrency patterns? peak concurrency is about 120 concurrent users for a given service, peak qps ~350. sustained lower load is fine.
[03:54] Liam O'Neill: we'll need to model both sustained and spike traffic. our plan: run steady-state soak for 30m at target rps, then spike tests to 2-3x to validate graceful degradation and failover to fallback models.
[04:10] Maya Chen: timeline wise, here's a suggested plan: week 0 (this week) collect scripts and token distributions; week 1 configure harness and run initial non-streaming runs; week 2 run streaming tests and warm-cache experiments; week 3 analyze results and tune model configs; week 4 decision/pilot wrap. does that align?
[04:32] Ravi Patel: that's reasonable. we may want an extra week for legal/security if we need private deployment or KMS integrations.
[04:41] Jordan Lee: about security — we'll need SOC2 docs and clarify KMS usage. can you provide details?
[04:48] Maya Chen: yes — we'll share our SOC2 report and a security overview. for KMS, if you use Private deployment we'll integrate customer-managed KMS; if Hosted we'll discuss envelope encryption and audit logs.
[05:01] Sofia Martinez: outstanding items: we need to ensure request replay fidelity — tokenization mismatch has caused differences in other vendor tests.
[05:11] Liam O'Neill: agree — that's why our runner tokenizes with the same tokenizer as the model and records token counts per operation. we'll include that in the runbook.
[05:23] Ravi Patel: how do you capture error rates and throttling behavior? we want to ensure no silent drops.
[05:30] Maya Chen: harness captures http status, model error codes, partial streams, and backpressure metrics. we'll surface retry rates and any 429 patterns.
[05:40] Sofia Martinez: for the non-streaming run, what sequence length should we set for the long tests? 2k tokens?
[05:46] Liam O'Neill: yes set to 2k for the long-RAG path. for short interactive set to 40/80. we'll need sample retrieval latencies if you want more realistic RAG timing.
[05:58] Jordan Lee: question — do you support VPC peering for Dedicated or Private? we may want to test in a Private environment if data residency is required.
[06:06] Maya Chen: Dedicated and Private both support VPC peering; Private includes customer-managed networking and can be on-prem if needed. we'll discuss provisioning details after this call.
[06:18] Speaker 2: (brief crosstalk)
[06:22] Maya Chen: ok next steps recap: Maya to send harness link and example Locust scripts; Sofia to upload scripts and token distributions; Liam to recommend instance/quantization options; Jordan to start networking/KMS prep. we'll aim for initial non-streaming run week of 3/30.
[06:41] Ravi Patel: perfect. any other competitors or tooling notes? we're also comparing to Anthropic and AWS managed endpoints on price/perf.
[06:51] Liam O'Neill: understood, we'll include comparable metrics where possible.
[06:55] Sofia Martinez: thanks all, we'll get the artifacts uploaded this week.
[07:00] Maya Chen: great, thanks everyone. end of call.

Notes: transcript contains occasional transcription errors and mis-attributions; timestamps approximate. Shared artifacts: Redwood benchmark harness repo (link to be shared), example Locust scripts, security overview deck.
